You are a Python test engineer. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge (detached at HEAD). Edit files here directly. NEVER git commit, never touch /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge itself, never run `uv`, never call a billed model or the network. FIRST run: [ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv ; run tests as `PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 0 <files>` (never pass --cov); ruff as `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check <files>` and `.venv/bin/python -m ruff format <files>` (line length 120, double quotes, Python 3.12).

BACKGROUND. The default story's data is moving from nine legacy files to a source tree that `storygame.story_source.compile_source_tree` compiles. The converted tree is now committed at data/stories/continuity-initiative/source/ (story.yaml, catalog.yaml, scenes/<id>.yaml and scenes/<id>.match.yaml). It was generated by `storygame.story_source.convert.write_source_tree(package, root)` from the legacy package `load_story_package(Path("data/stories/continuity-initiative"))`. The legacy loader ignores the source/ directory. Until the legacy files are removed, the committed tree must not drift from what the converter produces.

YOUR JOB: write ONE test file, tests/story_source/test_source_tree_drift.py, in the style of tests/story_source/test_parity_default.py (read it first). Tests:
1. `test_committed_source_tree_matches_a_fresh_conversion(tmp_path)`: convert the legacy package into tmp_path with write_source_tree, then assert the set of relative file paths equals the committed tree's and every file's bytes are equal. On failure the assertion message must list the missing, extra and differing paths (cap each list at 20) and say how to regenerate: run write_source_tree on the legacy package into data/stories/continuity-initiative/source.
2. `test_committed_source_tree_is_valid_and_compiles()`: `check_source_tree(committed)` returns no diagnostics (print them in the assertion message) and `compile_source_tree(committed)` returns a package with the same scene ids in the same order as the legacy package.
Use the Path constants relative to the repo root like the gate test does. No new dependencies. Do not edit any other file.

HARD LIMITS. Never edit existing tests, tests/shard_durations.json, docs/, the data files or anything under storygame/. If a test cannot pass without such an edit, write why in NOTES_r6a.txt (worktree root, never committed) and leave the test failing.
tasks.check:
set -eo pipefail
[ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp
out=$(mktemp)
rc=0
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 0 -rs tests/story_source/test_source_tree_drift.py > "$out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
tail -30 "$out"
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || exit "$rc"
if grep -E "SKIPPED" "$out"; then echo "a gate test skips"; exit 1; fi
n=$(grep -cE "^def test_" tests/story_source/test_source_tree_drift.py)
[ "$n" -ge 2 ] || { echo "expected at least 2 tests, found $n"; exit 1; }
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check tests/story_source/test_source_tree_drift.py
.venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check tests/story_source/test_source_tree_drift.py
git add -A -- storygame tests data
bad=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -v -e '^tests/story_source/test_source_tree_drift.py$' || true)
[ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "files outside ownership staged: $bad"; exit 1; }
git diff --cached > /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/story-data-round6a/r6a-drift.patch
test -s /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/story-data-round6a/r6a-drift.patch
